🇷🇸 Serbia's Student List demands mass resignations across security services, police and courts

At its first press conference since winning Sunday's snap parliamentary election, the Student List called for the immediate resignation of a long list of top officials it accuses of serving Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party rather than the state.

The list includes police director Dragan Vasiljević, Security Information Agency (civilian intelligence) director Vladimir Orlić, Military Security Agency director Maj. Gen. Đuro Jovanić and Constitutional Court president Vladan Petrov. They also want the heads of the criminal police, the Gendarmerie and the special anti-terrorist unit removed, saying the intelligence service acted as a "party" security service used to discredit political opponents.

The students want prosecutors to reopen a series of high-profile cases, including the deadly 2024 collapse of the Novi Sad railway station canopy and the 2018 murder of Kosovo Serb politician Oliver Ivanović. They also want audits of where the money went on major state projects, including Expo 2027, Belgrade Waterfront, the Rio Tinto lithium project and pandemic spending, plus a review of all public contracts.

At state broadcaster Radio Television of Serbia, the director and the news chief have already resigned at their demand, and they are now pushing out the deputy director. They also want Telekom Srbija director Vladimir Lučić removed. Mirjana Nikolić, a professor and Student List candidate, said a telecom operator should not act as "Serbia's editor-in-chief."

Staff in state institutions were urged to report any destruction of documents before the new government is formed, and a whistleblower email has been set up. "We did not come for revenge but to return the institutions to the citizens," said student Filip Ubović.

🇮🇹🇧🇦 Italian military helicopter crashes in Bosnia, 4 dead

An Italian Army CH-47F Chinook serving with the EU's military mission in Bosnia, EUFOR Althea, crashed on Thursday afternoon near the village of Gorice in the Brčko District, northeastern Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Four Italian servicemen were killed and 11 injured, according to EUFOR. Three died at the scene and a fourth died later in Brčko hospital. All 15 people on board were Italian. One of the injured is reported to be in critical condition and may be transferred to Tuzla.

Eyewitnesses said the helicopter was flying low and spun several times in the air before going down in an uninhabited area just short of the first houses in the village. Footage circulating online appears to show the Chinook rotating out of control as it descended.

EUFOR says the flight was a routine operation and has launched an investigation. Italy's Defence Ministry says the cause is still being established. EUFOR also urged locals not to spread "unverified information" and to rely only on official channels.
